item.title: LOT-169: App-wide text size slider and compact density

labels.name: status: ready
labels.description: Specified and ready to be picked

labels.name: host: mac

item.body:
### Summary

As a reader, I want to make the text smaller or bigger with a slider and choose a dense display, so that lists and topics show as much as the legacy Favoris list or Gmail's dense list instead of looking zoomed in.

Operator decision 2026-10-28: the renders shown so far look zoomed in and very big. There MUST be a text-size slider whose range goes below the current default, and a density option (compact rows). Respect Dynamic Type: the slider is an in-app offset on top of it; accessibility sizes still work.

### Scope

- **One app-wide type scale.** Every screen (sidebar / Catégories, topic lists, favourites and flags, MP list, settings, reader) takes its sizes from one scale: system text styles × the in-app percentage `text_size_percent` (70–130 %, step 5, stored by LOT-119 (#210), PR #292). No fixed point size outside the scale.
- **Reader:** the same percentage drives `reader.css` (`html` font size on top of `-apple-system-body`), live, without reloading the page. The text-size part of LOT-106 (#197) moves here; LOT-106 keeps layout, signatures and swipe.
- **Density:** `compact_mode` (LOT-119) switches lists to compact rows: smaller insets and row spacing, title on one or two lines, one meta line (author · replies · date), smaller flag / unread markers. References: Gmail dense list, legacy Favoris list (legacy `Common.swift:228` `compact_mode`, `compactListSectionSpacing` `:309`).
- **Default:** check the default (100 %, regular density) against the legacy app on the same device: row height and lines per screen in the Favoris and topic lists within ±10 % of legacy (screenshots of both on the PR, no real pseudo or topic title in them: use the anonymized fixtures or blur).
- **Dynamic Type:** the in-app percentage multiplies the system size; AX sizes still grow the text; the slider never stops large accessibility sizes from applying. `@ScaledMetric` for icon and spacing sizes.
- Legacy `text_size_scale` (100/110/120/130, `Common.swift:265-293`) is already migrated by LOT-119.

- Module: App · Difficulty: medium · Priority: high · post-MVP
- Implements: operator decision 2026-10-28 (A); absorbs FEAT-010 (#154) "compact mode" and the text-size part of LOT-106 (#197)
- Legacy sources (read-only, `origin/master`): `HFRswift/Swift/Common.swift:228` (`compact_mode`), `:265-293` (`AppTextSizeScale`), `:309` (`compactListSectionSpacing`), `MessagesView.swift` (`MessageBodyTextSizeCSS`)
- Spec: `docs/lots/LOT-169-*.md`

### Depends on

- LOT-119 (#210, in PR #292): stores `text_size_percent` and `compact_mode`
- LOT-082 (#100, done)
- LOT-083 (#101, done)

### Blocked by

none: every dependency is merged (unblocked 2026-10-29, steward ext/opus-helper1)

### Model

Sonnet → Opus (AGENTS.md §6: the reviewer is never the author model)

### Captures needed

- none (no HFR fact involved)

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Moving the slider resizes the text of every screen live, including an open topic (no reload); 70 % is visibly denser than today's default.
- [ ] Compact mode shows more rows per screen than regular mode in the topic, favourites and MP lists (measured, numbers on the PR).
- [ ] Default size and density compared with the legacy app (row height, rows per screen) on the PR, with anonymized screenshots.
- [ ] Dynamic Type AX1–AX5 still enlarge text at every slider value; nothing truncates into unreadability at 130 % + AX5.
- [ ] View logic lives in `@Observable @MainActor` models tested with Swift Testing in `App/SwiftHFRTests/`; each new test is shown to fail without the change.
- [ ] `xcodebuild build test` green on the iPhone 18 Pro and an iPad simulator (iOS 27.0), and the `App build + tests` CI job green.
- [ ] UI strings in French; light, dark and Dynamic Type XL checked; no new dependency.

### Before you start (agents and humans)

Read, in order: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/agents/ORCHESTRATION.md, docs/agents/REVIEW-ROUNDS.md, docs/agents/LESSONS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, App/README.md, ADR 0012, the spec of every dependency (docs/lots/), docs/HFR-PROTOCOL.md for any forum fact, docs/FIXTURES.md if captures are involved. Claim with `/claim <session-id>` on this issue before writing code; PR body `Closes #<this issue>` + `Claim: <session-id>`; never guess HFR behaviour (stop and list the captures needed).
